questions.q:
Match the following Maxwell's equations: (The symbols used here have their usual meanings)
List-I
(a) Gauss' law for electrostatics
(b) Gauss' law for magnetism
(c) Faraday's law
(d) Ampere-Maxwell's law
List-II
(i) $\oint \vec E \cdot d\vec A=\dfrac{Q}{\epsilon_0}$
(ii) $\oint \vec B \cdot d\vec l=\mu_0\left[i_c+\epsilon_0\dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}\right]$
(iii) $\oint \vec B \cdot d\vec A=0$
(iv) $\oint \vec E \cdot d\vec l=-\dfrac{d\phi_B}{dt}$
options: a - i, b - iii, c - iv, d - ii
a - ii, b - iii, c - i, d - iv
a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i
questions.explanation: Gauss' law for electrostatics is (i); Gauss' law for magnetism (no monopoles) is (iii); Faraday's law is (iv); the Ampere-Maxwell law is (ii).

questions.q: What range of electromagnetic spectrum is considered as light?
questions.explanation: Visible light lies roughly between 400 nm and 700 nm in the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: Match the following types of waves with their wavelength ranges. Waves: i. Microwave ii. Visible light iii. Ultraviolet iv. X-rays. Wavelength ranges: a) 700 nm to 400 nm b) 1 nm to $10^{-3}$ nm c) 0.1 m to 1mm d) 400 nm to 1nm
options: i – a, ii – d, iii – b, iv – c
i – c, ii – a, iii – d, iv – b
i – d, ii – b, iii – c, iv – a
i – b, ii – c, iii – a, iv – d
questions.explanation: Microwave: 0.1 m to 1 mm (c); visible light: 700-400 nm (a); ultraviolet: 400-1 nm (d); X-rays: 1 nm to $10^{-3}$ nm (b).

questions.q: The ratio of the magnitudes of electric field to the magnetic field of an electromagnetic wave is of the order of
questions.explanation: For an EM wave, E/B = c ≈ 3×10$^8$ ms$^{-1}$, of the order 10$^8$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Which of the following radiations of electromagnetic waves has the highest wavelength?
questions.explanation: In the electromagnetic spectrum, wavelength decreases in the order microwaves > IR > UV > X-rays, so microwaves have the highest wavelength among the given options.

questions.q: Suppose that the electric field amplitude of an electromagnetic wave is E$_0$ = 120 NC$^{-1}$ and its frequency is f = 50 MHz. Then which of the following value is incorrectly computed?
options: Angular frequency of EM wave is $\pi \times 10^8$ rad/s
Propagation constant (angular wave number) is 2.1 rad/m
Wavelength of the EM wave is 6 m.
questions.explanation: $B_0=E_0/c=400$ nT (correct); $\omega=2\pi f=\pi\times10^8$ rad/s (correct); $\lambda=c/f=6$ m (correct); but $k=\omega/c=\pi/3\approx1.05$ rad/m, not 2.1 rad/m, so (C) is incorrectly computed.

questions.q: The source of electromagnetic waves can be a charge.
options: Moving parallel to the magnetic field
questions.explanation: Only an accelerating charge radiates electromagnetic waves; a charge moving in a circular orbit is centripetally accelerated.

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave is travelling in x-direction with electric field vector given by, $\vec E_y = E_0\sin(kx-\omega t)\hat j$. The correct expression for magnetic field vector is
questions.explanation: For an EM wave travelling along x with E along y, B must be along z (since $\hat i = \hat j\times\hat k$) with amplitude $E_0/c$, so $\vec B_z = (E_0/C)\sin(kx-\omega t)\hat k$.

questions.q: If $\vec E$ and $\vec B$ represent electric and magnetic field vectors of an electromagnetic wave, the direction of propagation of the wave is along
questions.explanation: In an electromagnetic wave, $\vec E$, $\vec B$ and the direction of propagation are mutually perpendicular, with propagation along $\vec E \times \vec B$.

questions.q: Electromagnetic radiation used to sterilise milk is
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet (UV) rays are commonly used for sterilisation of milk and water.

questions.q: If $\varepsilon_0$ and $\mu_0$ are the permittivity and permeability of free space and $\varepsilon$ and $\mu$ are the corresponding quantities for a medium, then refractive index of the medium is
questions.explanation: Speed of light in the medium $v=1/\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}$ and in vacuum $c=1/\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}$; refractive index $n=c/v=\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon/(\mu_0\varepsilon_0)}$.

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency 20 MHz travels through a space along x direction. If the electric field vector at a certain point in space is 6 V m$^{-1}$, what is the magnetic field vector at that point?
X-rays, gamma rays and microwaves travelling in vacuum have
questions.explanation: All electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light c in vacuum, but X-rays, gamma rays and microwaves differ in wavelength (and hence frequency).

questions.q: Electromagnetic wave consists of periodically oscillating electric and magnetic vectors .................
options: in randomly oriented planes but vibrating in phase.
in mutually perpendicular planes but vibrating in phase.
in mutually perpendicular planes but vibrating with a phase difference of $\pi$
in mutually perpendicular planes but vibrating with a phase difference of $\pi/2$
questions.explanation: In an electromagnetic wave, $\vec E$ and $\vec B$ oscillate in mutually perpendicular planes and are in phase with each other.
